lead: Brent Crude / BZ=F — one push from the hundred-dollar barrel
smaller: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — the ticket paid, then the app crashed
SoFi Technologies / SOFI — a billion-dollar bet on one-stop banking
AMC Entertainment / AMC — meme veterans count scars in a correction
why_lead: The 22 February session turned the Russia threat into policy and the oil price into a round-number chase: Brent 96.84 USD/bbl, +3.53% on the day and +12.25% over 20 sessions, TTF gas +8.17%, wheat +5.93%, with S&P 500 -1.01% and VIX 28.81. Newly published evidence: oil 'nearing $100' (NYT n1109, Guardian n1263, NPR n1264, BBC n1275), Germany freezing Nord Stream 2 (Reuters n1099, Guardian n1101), new US and UK sanctions (Al Jazeera n1255, GOV.UK n1272), Sberbank/VTB rebounding as top banks escaped UK sanctions (n0764), consumer-facing coverage (LA Times n1274, Kiplinger n1605) and Bloomberg's Covid-crash-to-$100 analog (n0082). Relation to earlier notes: oil appeared as a smaller USO item on 15 February (seven-year-high war barrel, producer non-confirmation) and Exxon on 2 and 8 February; this is a material update with a new catalyst set (Nord Stream halt, first sanctions tranche, $100 headlines) and a different analog, promoted to lead because it is the day's dominant crowd narrative. DWAC, the 21 and 22 February lead, is demoted to a secondary item to avoid a third consecutive DWAC lead. No outcome after the cutoff (invasion, later sanctions, later prices) is used; the pending RBNZ, Lowe's, TJX, Lucid and eBay events are not referenced.
why_smaller: Digital World Acquisition: material update to the 21-22 February leads, kept secondary. New evidence is the first post-launch trading session (DWAC 92.90 USD, +10.18%, +38.22% 20s) and newly published coverage: Reuters on the SPAC's surge as Truth Social topped downloads (n0780), Apptopia's 170k downloads (n1604), CNBC's chart-topping report (n1611), The Week's 13-hour crash (n1609) and Bloomberg's Dubsmash story as the cautionary analog (n1603).

SoFi Technologies: a new, distinct fintech narrative not used in earlier notes. SOFI fell 9.92% to 10.26 USD (-22.86% 20s) on the day it agreed to buy Technisys for $1.1B (Banking Dive n0771, American Banker one-stop-shop n0769), with HOOD -15.28% and SQ -15.88% over five sessions and the 2Y at 1.56% (+57 bps 20 obs) as the break conditions. Earlier fintech items were PayPal (2 February) and Affirm (14 February).

AMC Entertainment: the meme crowd's endurance narrative, refreshed by new 22 February attention evidence (Time's 'I'm down 20 grand, but I'm still up' meme-trading retrospective n0675, WSJ+ GameStop/Reddit event n0739) and a -7.99% AMC session in a confirmed S&P 500 correction (Reuters n1924, CNBC n0711). Relation to earlier notes: GameStop led on 1 February and AMC was a smaller item on 9 and 14 February on company and rally catalysts; this item is a material update centred on the GME/AMC divergence (GME +17.88% vs AMC -1.02% over 20 sessions).
considered_not_chosen: Home Depot (-8.85% to 316.17 USD on a margin warning, Reuters n0985, CNN n0725, CNBC n0984): large drop with good coverage, but weaker retail-crowd evidence; Lowe's results are pending on the report date and were not referenced.

Defense (LMT -0.07% to 386.20 USD, ITA -1.38%, Rheinmetall +2.20%): the 22 February smaller item's trigger (holding above 386.46 USD) was not met, but there is no newly published defense-stock evidence, so no carryover.

Bitcoin (+3.27% to 38,286.03 USD while COIN -6.56%, MARA -5.69%, BITO -5.26%) and Coinbase backpedalling over its Super Bowl ad (n0126): crypto already appeared on 8, 9, 14, 15 and 21 February; not repeated without a new crowd catalyst.
Ford (-4.16% to 17.29 USD, giving back the 18 February gain flagged on 22 February): no new own-date Ford evidence, so not carried over.
Wheat (+5.93% to 844.25 US cents/bu; Marketplace n1724): folded into the oil lead as part of the commodity spillover rather than given its own slot.

Avoided as wording or timing risks: n1104 (New York Post headline describing an 'invasion' for the 22 February deployment) and n1255's 'beginning invasion' quote (cited only for the sanctions it reports); no RBNZ, Lowe's, TJX, Lucid or eBay outcome headlines were used because those events fall on 23 February.
